summary: Requests updates to monitor host tables, in conjunction with moving NIC users to the OFFICE-1 computer. It relates to RFCs 621 and 609.

eli5.summary: The NIC was moving to a different computer, so everyone was asked to update their lists.

subtitle: Update network host tables as NIC services move to OFFICE-1

tldr.problem: The NIC (Network Information Center) was moving its services from SRI-ARC to a new computer called OFFICE-1, making the existing network host tables outdated.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 620 requests that all ARPANET sites update their monitor host tables to reflect the new location: site 53 (octal) now points to OFFICE-1, while site 2 remains SRI-ARC but is renamed to ARC. The NIC nickname should now refer to OFFICE-1.
tldr.outcome: Network sites updated their tables so that users accessing NIC services would automatically connect to the correct location.

today: RFC 620 documents a routine administrative change in the early ARPANET. It reflects how network coordination was managed when infrastructure moved between sites.

sections.title: NIC Relocation
sections.content:
The Network Information Center (NIC) had been operating at SRI-ARC but was moving to a new facility called OFFICE-1. To ensure network users could reach NIC services, all sites needed to update their monitor host tables, which map host names to network addresses.

The change was to take effect on Friday, March 8, 1974. RFC 620 specifies exactly what entries should be added or modified in these tables.
sections.eli5: When the NIC moved to a new computer, everyone on the network had to update their address books.

sections.title: Table Updates
sections.content:
TENEX sites should update their host tables to contain three entries: one for SRI-ARC at site 2, one for OFFICE-1 at site 53 (octal), and one for TYMSHARE-TIP at site 253. The nickname section should be updated so that 'ARC' refers to SRI-ARC and 'NIC' refers to OFFICE-1.

Non-TENEX sites should make equivalent changes using their own system's conventions for host management.
sections.eli5: Each computer needed to change its list so that 'NIC' pointed to the new building, not the old one.

sections.title: Service Continuity
sections.content: With these changes, NIC users would be automatically directed to OFFICE-1 when accessing services by the 'NIC' hostname. The ARC nickname would now refer to the remaining services at SRI-ARC for those who needed them.
sections.eli5: After the change, asking for 'NIC' got you to the new building, where all the services now were.

references.text: Kudlick, M., "NIC User Directories at SRI ARC", RFC 621, March 1974.
